**Finding: missing (high severity) — Termination for convenience (T4C)**

The Agreement locks a three-year term (§8.1) with automatic 12-month renewals (§8.2), but Section 9 contains only:
- §9.1 material breach (either Party, 30-day cure)
- §9.2 insolvency (either Party)
- §9.3 Customer trigger-based rights (security incident, SLA misses, unlawfulness, infringement)
- §9.5 severability of Order Form terminations

Other termination hooks (§6.2 failed acceptance, §19.4 warranty, §20.5 infringement, §27.3 force majeure) are all remedy-based, not convenience. There is no general Customer right to exit without cause anywhere in the document — walk-away territory for a multi-year commitment, failing both the preferred and fallback positions.

Mitigating point noted in the rationale: Vendor likewise has no convenience right, so no deletion was needed.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** new §9.4 inserted after §9.3 giving us termination for convenience of the Agreement or any Order Form, in whole or in part, on 30 days' written notice, without penalty or early-termination fee, with a refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and confirming Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right. The comment offers 60 days' notice as a fallback.
